title: Imitation (I.1)
hook: anyone can copy a star's haircut; the Imitation of Christ opens on following, not copying
tomorrow: can you know exactly what sorry means and never feel it?

segments.voice: A week of lines, from the end of one book to the start of another. Give what you ask. If no one asks. In charity. A sabbath without evening. Sorrow and praise. And yesterday, a small book: a book for beginners.
screen: `GIVE WHAT YOU ASK · IF NO ONE ASKS · IN CHARITY.` → `A SABBATH WITHOUT EVENING · SORROW AND PRAISE.` → `A BOOK FOR BEGINNERS.`

segments.voice: Anybody can copy a star's haircut, or the song they walk out to. That's copying. Following is something else: taking on how they train, what they care about, where they go when nobody's filming. The Imitation of Christ opens on that difference. Its first line is from the Gospel of John, in the Douay-Rheims: "he that followeth me, walketh not in darkness."
screen: `COPY THE HAIRCUT.` → `OR FOLLOW THE WAY.` → `HE THAT FOLLOWETH ME.`

segments.voice: Then the book explains itself. These are the words of Christ, it says, telling us to imitate his life and his ways if we want to be truly enlightened and free of blindness of heart. So the first thing to study, it says, is the life of Jesus. Not a costume, not a pose. A life to learn by heart until it shapes yours. That's the word today, and it's lighter than it sounds. Imitation in this book doesn't mean a copy. It means following, step after step, the way a child learns a family's way of laughing without a manual. And notice how this week's lines lead into it. Augustine asked God for the strength to do what God asks. He admitted some things you know only by living them. He argued in charity, rested in God, owned up and praised. A book for beginners now names the beginning: follow.
screen: `THE WORDS OF CHRIST, FIRST.` · `STUDY HIS LIFE.` · `NOT A COPY: FOLLOWING.` · `THIS WEEK, LEADING HERE.` · then, large: `FOLLOW.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one small thing Jesus does in the Gospels: noticing someone overlooked, sharing a meal, speaking kindly to a stranger. Then picture one person you'll see tomorrow, and choose the one small act you could follow him in, and let the choice settle.
Imitation. In this book, not copying a look but following a life: the life of Jesus, studied until it shapes yours.
Your line: follow. One word, and a whole week of lines already walking in that direction. Good night.
